name: strategy_research_catalog_v1
purpose: Track credible public/practitioner strategy families before implementation, replication, optimization, and paper promotion.
selection_principles: Prefer systems with explicit rules, long samples, cross-market evidence, or public replication targets.
Separate robust strategy families from single-indicator ideas.
Require data-readiness and cost-readiness before promoting a strategy into paper trading.
Treat recent high-performing claims as research leads, not proof, until reproduced in this codebase.

candidates.label: Diversified time-series momentum / managed futures
candidates.core_idea: Trade assets in the direction of their own medium-term trends across asset classes, with volatility targeting and portfolio risk budgets.
candidates.why_it_matters: Among the best-documented systematic anomalies, with evidence across commodities, currencies, equity indices, and bonds over long samples.
implementation_notes: Use multiple lookbacks such as 1, 3, 6, and 12 months.
Normalize signals by realized volatility.
Allocate by asset-class risk budgets and correlation scaling.
Evaluate crisis alpha, whipsaw sensitivity, turnover, and choppy-regime drawdowns.
Initial single-symbol strategy MVP exists as managedFuturesMomentum; portfolio-level risk budgets, correlation scaling, and crisis-alpha reporting still need allocator/reporting promotion.

candidates.label: Adaptive crypto trend following
candidates.core_idea: Use shorter-interval crypto trend signals, volatility-regime trailing stops, rolling Sharpe asset selection, and asymmetric long/short exposure.
candidates.why_it_matters: Recent crypto research reports strong out-of-sample risk-adjusted results when trend following is paired with adaptive portfolio construction.
implementation_notes: Use 4h/6h/1d bars depending on provider support.
Select liquid assets by rolling Sharpe and volume/liquidity filters.
Use volatility-calibrated trailing exits.
Limit short exposure because crypto spot availability and borrow mechanics differ by venue.
Initial MVP exists through cryptoAdaptiveTrend and select_crypto_adaptive_universe.

candidates.label: Style premia rotation: momentum, value, quality, defensive, carry
candidates.core_idea: Rank and allocate across securities or ETFs using diversified factor signals rather than isolated price indicators.
candidates.why_it_matters: Large quant managers emphasize diversified style premia instead of relying on a single signal family.
implementation_notes: Start with ETF proxies while fundamental data support is limited.
Use price momentum, low-volatility/defensive, dividend/carry proxies, and quality proxies where available.
Report factor crowding, regime sensitivity, and benchmark-relative value.
Initial cross-sectional ranking MVP exists through build_style_premia_ranking using OHLCV proxies plus optional carry/yield columns.
data_requirements: fundamental data or ETF factor proxies

candidates.label: Graph-cluster statistical arbitrage
candidates.core_idea: Discover related equity clusters, build beta/sector-neutral spreads, trade spread mean reversion with stability and cost gates.
candidates.why_it_matters: Current statistical-arbitrage research emphasizes scalable multi-pair portfolios, clustering, and ML-assisted signal/risk filters.
implementation_notes: Start with ETF/large-cap pairs before broad universe stat-arb.
Add rolling correlation, cointegration, z-score, half-life, and spread stationarity reports.
Require beta neutrality, borrow availability, transaction cost estimates, and stop-loss/take-profit optimization.
Initial dependency-light pair discovery MVP exists through discover_stat_arb_pairs with a cointegration proxy; formal Engle-Granger/ADF testing remains future work.

candidates.label: Volatility risk premium / systematic option income
candidates.core_idea: Harvest implied-vs-realized volatility premia using dynamically sized short option exposure with strict crash controls.
candidates.why_it_matters: Volatility selling is a major institutional strategy family, but it requires options-specific modeling before it is safe to test.
implementation_notes: Do not implement as an equity-bar hack.
Add options chains, IV surfaces, Greeks, assignment/exercise, option margin, and tail-risk stress first.
Study VIX/Kelly/hybrid sizing and drawdown controls.
Promotion gate exists through evaluate_options_promotion_gate; actual option-income strategies remain blocked until every required options capability passes.

candidates.label: Dynamic growth/defensive allocation overlay
candidates.core_idea: Rotate between growth/risk assets and defensive/cash/income assets using smooth macro-market timing scores.
candidates.why_it_matters: Recent research suggests interpretable smooth allocation can reduce drawdowns and improve risk-adjusted performance, even when raw CAGR does not always beat high-growth static exposure.
implementation_notes: Use continuous scores rather than hard binary regimes.
Inputs can include rate trend, SPY drawdown, volatility relief, growth crowding, and liquidity proxies.
Compare to static growth, static defensive, SPY, and volatility-matched benchmarks.
Initial MVP exists through build_dynamic_allocation with smooth trend, drawdown, volatility, rates, and liquidity stress scores.

candidates.label: Trend following on sectors, factors, and yield-curve shape
candidates.core_idea: Apply trend logic to factor spreads, sector baskets, value-vs-growth, low-volatility-vs-high-beta, and yield-curve-shape trades.
candidates.why_it_matters: Practitioners increasingly discuss trend following beyond simple asset direction, including factor trends and curve-shape trends.
implementation_notes: Start with ETF spread proxies.
Use market-neutral relative baskets where possible.
Validate that signal returns are not just hidden market beta.
Initial MVP exists through build_factor_trend_report using normalized ETF proxy spreads.

candidates.label: Market making / short-horizon liquidity provision
candidates.core_idea: Quote bid/ask spreads and manage inventory around microstructure signals.
candidates.why_it_matters: Top-tier in industry, but fundamentally a different data/execution problem from daily-bar backtesting.
implementation_notes: Requires order book data, queue position, latency modeling, quote updates, adverse selection models, and exchange/broker fee modeling.
Do not evaluate with the current bar-based engine.
